transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I’m having trouble keeping my mind on what I’m supposed to be doing at work. In the lab, even during a grant call or a safety meeting, some little thing catches me—a pump noise, a side comment, an odd peak in old data—and then I’m off on that for hours. Meanwhile the actual thing people need from me just… doesn’t get done.
Do you also find yourself getting distracted or having trouble focusing on tasks outside of work, like at home or during conversations?

Yes. It’s not just at work. If I’m talking to someone, something they say can send me off on a completely different track, and I lose the thread. At home it’s similar—I’ll start one thing and then notice some small detail, and hours can go by before I realize I never finished what I meant to do.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to be moving or doing something, even when you’re trying to relax or focus on a task?

Yes. I get… keyed up, I guess. I’ll go into the lab before anyone else is there and start rewriting protocols, moving instrument schedules around, emailing people in different countries, opening new analyses all at once. Sitting still feels like I’m wasting time, like I need to fix everything while I can.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are racing so much that it's hard to keep up with them, like one idea quickly leads to another before you can finish the first?
I don’t know if I’d call it racing. It’s more like… one thing leads to another and I’m already somewhere else before I notice. But I’m not sure how to describe it.
Looking back, did you have similar issues with staying focused or feeling restless when you were a child, maybe even back in school?
I’m not really sure. I mean, school was a long time ago. I don’t remember it being talked about as a problem, but… I don’t know if I’m remembering it clearly.

Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or so confident that you didn’t need much sleep, and you took on a lot of projects or felt like you could do things faster or better than others?

Yes… there have been times like that. I thought I could basically pull the whole multi-site project back together myself. Redesign the spectroscopy approach, fix everyone’s work, mentor the students better than their own advisors, and still make the grant deadline.

At the time it didn’t feel unrealistic. It felt like people were just… slowing me down.

Have there been times when you felt unusually good, almost euphoric, or unusually irritable for several days in a row, where you didn’t feel like you needed much sleep and were doing or planning a lot of activities?

Yes. For months, honestly, it’s felt like the lab is finally… moving at my speed. Almost electrified.

But if someone questions the plan or tells me to slow down, I don’t handle it well. I snap. Enough that some of the students seem to avoid my office now.
Have there been times when you felt down or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know. Not really in a way I’d call that. I’ve had rough days, sure, but… I don’t think it’s been most of the day, nearly every day.
